title: Information Templates: A New Paradigm for Intelligent Active Feature Acquisition
claim: A sequential acquisition policy gathers features step by step, with its prediction sharpening until it is confident enough to stop and decide.
layout: 2 side-by-side examples, each with a top row of observations and a bottom row of probability bars, left-to-right over time
description: The figure shows two rollouts of an active feature acquisition policy on handwritten digits, a 4 on the left and an 8 on the right. Each example begins with the original 16x16 grayscale digit image. Next to it are three columns of snapshots (step 0, a middle step, and terminate). The top row shows the observation as a cyan canvas where the acquired pixels appear as black, gray or white squares. The canvas is nearly empty at step 0 and fills in with scattered pixels over time. The bottom row has bar charts of class probabilities over digits 0-9. At step 0 the distribution is nearly uniform. By termination it concentrates on the true class, near 4 for the first example and at 8 for the second, where the peak is very sharp. The eye goes first to the cyan observation panels.
caption: Example of rolling out an AFA policy. The AFA agent continues gathering information until it has enough information to make a decision about the instance at hand.
abstract: Active feature acquisition (AFA) is an instance-adaptive paradigm in which, at inference time, a policy sequentially chooses which features to acquire (at a cost) before predicting. Existing approaches either train reinforcement learning policies, which deal with a difficult MDP, or greedy policies that cannot account for the joint informativeness of features or require knowledge about the underlying data distribution. To overcome this, we propose Template-based AFA (TAFA), a non-greedy framework that learns a small library of feature templates -- sets of features that are jointly informative -- and uses this library of templates to guide the next feature acquisitions. Through identifying feature templates, the proposed framework not only significantly reduces the action space considered by the policy but also alleviates the need to estimate the underlying data distribution. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that TAFA outperforms the existing state-of-the-art baselines while achieving lower overall acquisition cost and computation.
